_scenario: One PhysicsWorld — "2d" on Rapier2dAdapter, §32 sleeping left at its default (ON, as examples/blending leaves it) — tracked on ONE PhysicsSystem inside ONE Application that also registers an AnimationSystem (§39 step 3) and createPoseTargetCaptureSystem (§39 step 3 − 1), stepped 600 clean fixed frames of 1/60 s (10 s, exactly one fixed step each, nothing dropped, §43 pose interpolation off). The scene is examples/blending's, restated: a static anchor block at (-5.6, 1.8) with NO collider, a static ground slab whose top is y = -2.7, and a three-link chain of "blended" nodes (§42) each carrying the §19 trio — a RigidBody, a rectangle Collider of half extents (0.17, 0.8) offset one half-length down so the leaf hangs below its proximal joint, and a PoseTarget — hinged anchor→link0→link1→link2 by three §28 HingeJoints. Each link's PoseTarget is driven by an AnimationMixer playing a looping 48-key clip sampled from the chain's own forward kinematics: aᵢ(t) = π/2 + 0.18·sin(2πt/3.6 − i), so every hinge is satisfied exactly at every key. Scripted §19 mode cycle at fixed steps: ANIMATED ("kinematic-position", weights physics 0 / animation 1) for steps 1–149; setBodyControlMode("dynamic", { inheritVelocityFrom }) on every link plus weights 1 / 0 on step 150 (switch 1, the ragdoll activation); RAGDOLL for steps 150–299; the §19 weight sweep on steps 300–389, one notch per step, BOTH weights written as (1 − w, w) with w = i/90 so the published animation share is exactly w; step 390 runs at w = 1 with the links still dynamic; setBodyControlMode("kinematic-position") plus weights 0 / 1 on step 391 (switch 2); ANIMATED again for steps 391–600. The wave keeps playing throughout — the targets are never re-seeded from where the ragdoll landed — so the recovery is a genuine metres-wide crossfade, which is what maxTargetGapMicro and maxStepRecoveringMicro measure. The per-step digest is the D6 FNV-1a hash of world.checksum() followed by each link node's PUBLISHED pose (position x, y, z then rotation x, y, z, w, in registration order): §33's solver checksum alone cannot see §19's blend output, which is the whole subject of this phase. summaryDigest is the same hasher over all 600 per-step digests in step order. Every "Micro" field is an integer count of 1e-6 units: micrometres for a distance, micrometres per second for a speed, millionths for a §19 weight.
_tier: same-runtime (§33). Rapier is compiled WebAssembly, so its arithmetic does not vary with the host JS engine's Math library, and §19's blend itself is plain IEEE-754 lerp/slerp — but cross-platform determinism is NOT claimed here: values cross the JS/wasm boundary as f64 → f32, the wasm image is pinned per platform by the package manager, and §33's cross-platform tier requires evidence this suite does not gather. The checksum algorithm itself is exact and cross-platform; only its inputs are runtime-bound.
